facts.fact: The Minister of State for Health said the National Digital Health Blueprint implementation has put at least 7.2 million Nigerians on the National Health Information Exchange Platform.

The Minister of State for Health described a National Health Information Exchange Platform with at least 7.2 million Nigerians registered on it, and separately said over 200 hospitals are integrated with Electronic Medical Records systems and mHealth initiatives; as_of is the document's published date, none being given.

The Minister said the ministry will continue scaling up technology-enabled platforms to deliver a National Health Information Exchange System connecting public and private, tertiary, secondary and primary health facilities.

facts.fact: NCDC, the Healthcare Federation of Nigeria and PharmAccess signed a memorandum framing a pilot of automated private-sector IDSR reporting into NCDC's SORMAS surveillance system, to test interoperable approaches; no facilities or start date are given.

facts.fact: The Health Care Providers Association of Nigeria launched HCPAN Connect, a platform meant to let providers, HMOs, regulators, government and patients exchange and aggregate health data in a central repository, to roll out from Lagos to other cities.
The HMCAN chairman said health data in Nigeria is fragmented across systems that do not speak to one another, with no point of connection.

systems.tiers: private providers, HMOs, regulators; Lagos first

facts.fact: The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare's architecture document says Nigeria lacks health data standards and a functional health information exchange, that no national health information exchange brings health data together, and that health information stays in the system where it is generated; no date is given for the statement, so the document's publication date is used.

facts.fact: The document says the National Council on Health approved in 2024 the creation and implementation of the Nigeria Digital in Health Initiative, to build a unified, interoperable health data and services infrastructure, with the Nigeria Digital Health Architecture (a federal HIE with shared health record, health claims exchange and health services exchange) as its third pillar and the HIE still to be built and operated by the NDHTO.

facts.fact: The Federal Ministry of Health says the Nigeria Digital Health Initiative, launched in March 2024 and endorsed by the National Council on Health in November 2024, includes a Health Information Exchange for data sharing across public and private facilities, to unify DHIS2, SORMAS, NHIA systems, LMIS and electronic medical records, for delivery before May 2027.
